name: libxsmm-full512-padded-288-byte-a-slices
hypothesis: Implement only the swarm-selected 288-byte packed-A K-slice layout in the unchanged NN baseline. Allocate 147456 bytes and pack 512 slices, each containing 256 data bytes followed by 32 unused bytes. Both scratch consumers advance by 288 bytes and rewind by 147456 bytes. The second row half remains at offset 128; the final data byte is at offset 147423, within the allocation. Parameter slots remain [4]=original B, [10]=original A, [16]=original C. This differs from the measured 272-byte layout. The hypothesis is that a different scratch address pattern changes cache conflicts; cache-set geometry and performance benefit are unverified. The extra 16 KiB can cause a regression. FP32 accumulation order, input preservation, output stores, SME transitions, general-size fallback, allocation-failure behavior, ABI and complete BSD notices remain unchanged. All packing remains inside the timed gemm call. No tools or tests were run. Require compilation and correctness checks at tolerance 0.002, including both row halves, fresh inputs, full overwrite, general sizes, tails and n<=0. Measure ten validation reports and ten fresh alternating paired controls with the initial power source and settings unchanged, preserving best-of-three timing. Report spread and comparisons against fresh same-mode peaks and the historical AC Automatic peak 1685.6230608449698; retain Battery Automatic peak 1668.5964359101147 separately. Comparator policy remains pending. Adoption requires min(candidate)>1.05*max(paired controls) and the unchanged held-out check. No speedup, causal effect or goal completion is established.
